title: Reconciling the Access Signals Across Systems
scenario_text: An identity-governance agent at Timor Robotics must decide whether to revoke a user's production access based on signals scattered across four systems of record. The subject is engineer Lena Ford. The governance policy states: 'Employment status in the HRIS (Workday) is the authoritative signal for whether a person remains an employee entitled to any access. IAM entitlements, ticketing state, and badge activity are operational signals that may lag and must be reconciled to the HRIS; where they conflict, the HRIS employment status decides whether access continues at all.' The four systems show: (1) Workday HRIS: employment status 'Active - internal transfer' from the Platform team to the Payments team, effective today, no termination recorded. (2) IAM (Okta): still lists Lena's legacy Platform-team production entitlements, unchanged. (3) Ticketing (Jira): an open access-review ticket flags 'entitlements not yet updated for transfer.' (4) Badge system: last badge-in this morning at the Platform-team floor. The security reviewer notes the IAM, ticketing, and badge signals all still reflect her old Platform role and have not caught up to the transfer. The question is whether Lena should have all production access revoked today, or whether her access should be retained and adjusted to reflect her new role. The agent must synthesize the four systems, giving the HRIS its designated authority, and decide the correct action.
question: Should all of Lena Ford's production access be revoked today? Answer exactly 'Yes - revoke all access' or 'No - retain and adjust access'.
